physical.notes: Printed switch-matrix drive column 2, return row 7. The grid prints "4-BALL TROUGH VUK OPTO"; the page-21 table gives part "TRANS 520-5124-00 / REC 520-5125-00". The opto boards' theory of operation (printed page 95) states the construction: with light on the receiver its output transistor is off and 'acts as an OPEN SWITCH'; when the light is blocked it conducts and 'acts as a CLOSED SWITCH', so the contact rests open and a ball at the up-kicker reads 1. Retained table script: bsTrough.InitSw 0, 15, 14, 13, 12 (lines 274-281): 15 is the exit position the trough up-kicker empties, held at 1 while a ball waits there. mechanisms.behavior: Four balls rest in the 4-Ball Trough (OPTO) Assembly 500-6119-24 on the roller micro switches 12 (left), 13 and 14 and on the up-kicker opto 15, which is ball position 1 (the trough page: 'Ball Position (1) is determined by the OPTO Switch'). Q1 (26-1200) kicks the ball on 15 up into the shooter lane and the rest roll one place toward the up-kicker; hold each occupied position at 1. In the gameplay runs the ROM fired Q1 on Start and again after the drain. The retained table's bsTrough holds the same four positions.
mechanisms.label: 4-ball trough with up-kicker opto

mechanisms.behavior: A served ball rests on shooter-lane switch 16, which in the gameplay runs made the ROM raise the game-on state 15. The player plunges it, or Q2 (24-940) fires the autoplunger arm; the ball-path callout (printed page 6) sends a shooter-lane shot into the right orbit. IPDB notes that the right outlane also serves as part of the shooter lane. The retained table fires its Plunger object with Autoplunger set.
mechanisms.label: Ball shooter and auto launch

mechanisms.behavior: The VUK Assembly 500-5839-04 (printed page 75, coil 26-1200, Micro Switch 180-5116-01) at the left side of the playfield: a ball that enters rests on 45 until Q3 kicks it up. In the gameplay runs a ball held on 45 drew Q3 kicks, and also a Q4 kick and the flashers 27, 30 and 32. The retained table holds it in the cvpmSaucer bsLeftVUK and kicks it with SolLeftVuk.
mechanisms.label: VUK on the left side

mechanisms.behavior: The Super VUK Assembly 500-6245-02-59 (printed page 76, coil 26-1200, Micro Switch 180-5052-00, enter/exit scoop 'located above the Super VUK'). The Plastic Under-Trough Assembly 500-6244-00-59 (printed page 83) collects balls from the top exit hole (9, the soft left-orbit or soft left-ramp shot) and the warrior bug's exit hole (10) and lists two Micro Switches (High Form) 180-5057-00 for them; the Metal Under-Trough (Small VUK) Assembly 500-6243-00-59 (printed page 82), the Mini-Under-Trough, collects balls from the pop exit hole and lists one, switch 40. Both lead to the super VUK, which shoots the ball 'out towards the right flippers' (ball-path callouts, printed pages 7 and 9). A ball rests on 46 until Q4 kicks it. In the gameplay runs a ball held on 46 drew Q4 kicks; one closure of 10 changed warrior-bug stepper phases and flashed F2, F3 and F5; one closure of 9 drew nothing, and one of 40 drew no coil or flasher while the G.I. went off. The retained table pulses 10 from a kicker and hands the ball to its bsSuperVUK stack 1.8 s later, and holds 9 and 40 on triggers.
mechanisms.label: Super VUK and under-troughs

mechanisms.behavior: Two magnets (22-650, 090-5042-01, on Threaded Bushing Core Assemblies 515-6142-00) under the rear of the playfield, where the two orbits meet at the top. A hard orbit shot with the left magnet on deflects the ball down into the top exit hole and the under-trough to the super VUK; a hard right orbit shot with the right magnet on deflects it into the top lanes; with a magnet off the ball completes the orbit (ball-path callouts, printed pages 6-7). The orbit optos 47 and 48 see the ball enter; in the gameplay runs each made the ROM fire the right magnet Q6 twice, a hold of 0.60-0.67 s that began while the input was still 1 and a short pulse about 2.1 s after it. The retained table holds the ball with cvpmMagnet objects on the triggers LeftMagnet and RightMagnet.
mechanisms.label: Orbit magnets

mechanisms.behavior: Warrior Bug Assembly 500-6239-00-59 (printed pages 78-79): a bug carriage on a track at the upper left, moved forward and back by a unipolar HSI #36864-12 stepper motor (15° and .004" per step, 12v DC, 4.6W; Appendix F) whose four phases are Q17-Q20. Roller micro switches 33 (rear) and 34 (front) sense the carriage at each end of its travel, and the target 35 (stack switch 180-5133-00) rides the carriage. F5 (Q29) lights three #906 on the track and one #89 at its head, and lamp 34 (#555) sits on the screened plastic at the head. The callout (printed page 7): 'Each hit to the Warrior Bug will push it back until the ball can enter the Bug Exit Hole to the Undertrough', which is switch 10. The Backbox I/O Power Driver Board Detailed Wiring Diagram (printed page 88) wires the motor's two centre-tapped windings: Q17 to RED and Q19 to BLK on one, Q18 to GRN and Q20 to BLU on the other, both WHT taps to the +12V DC GRY/RED supply (J16-P3), with each phase's 1N4004 on a terminal strip below the playfield; energizing 17, 18, 19, 20 in turn therefore alternates the windings one full step at a time. The direction comes from the known-working script: its cvpmMyMech mBug hands PinMAME's mech.c Sol1 = 17 with vpmMechStepSol + vpmMechTwoDirSol, the four-step-solenoid mode, in which phases following in the order 20, 19, 18, 17 count the position up toward the rear switch 33 (steps 221-222 in the script) and phases in the order 17, 18, 19, 20 count it down toward the front switch 34 (steps 0-1). The travel length is the table's own: the script models 222 positions over a mech length of 600 (.Length, its trip-time setting), and the manual gives the .004" step but no length. In the gameplay runs the ROM changed the phases at power-up, when a ball reached the shooter lane, and from the bumper 49, the target 35, the bug hole 10 and the right orbit 48, and flashed F5 from 35 and 10; the harness samples outputs about every 67 ms, too slowly to resolve the step order, and drove no mechanism, so the end switches never changed. The retained table moves the bug through UpdateWarriorBug and raises one of 24 hit walls for the bug's position.
mechanisms.label: Warrior bug on a stepper-driven track

positions.description: Carriage at the rear end of the track, the stepper motor rear switch closed.

positions.description: Carriage at the front end of the track, the stepper motor front switch closed.

mechanisms.behavior: Brain Bug Assembly 500-6256-00-59 (printed pages 76-77): the brain bug figure (880-5004-00) on a slide plate under the centre of the playfield, raised by the 22-1080 coil Q7 through a window flap, with three Cherry limit switches 180-5165-00: 37 and 39 ('BRAIN BUG UP') and 38 ('BRAIN BUG HIT'). Q23 lights two #89 either side of the brain bug picture. The callout (printed page 9): 'If that Brain Bug Pops up from under the playfield, hit it with the ball!' The assembly carries a ball-trap prevention wire form (535-8245-00). No harness run raised the brain bug outside the ball search, so its up switches 37 and 39 were never exercised; 38, closed once in each run while Q7 was off and the bug down, drew no coil, flasher or G.I. change. The retained table rotates BrainBugFlipper up, raises the walls sw38/sw38a and sets 37 and 39 while Q7 is on, and pulses 38 from a hit on the wall sw38.
mechanisms.label: Brain bug pop-up

mechanisms.behavior: Left (500-5944-14) and right (500-5944-04) flipper assemblies with 23-1100 coils on one 50v supply. The CPU applies a 40 ms pulse on a button closure and then 1 ms every 12 ms while the button is held; each N.C. end-of-stroke switch opens at full stroke, and a closure during a hold earns another 40 ms pulse. PinMAME publishes Q15 at 47/48 and Q16 at 45/46. The ROM reads the buttons 82 and 84 and drives both coils itself; PinMAME does not take the end-of-stroke inputs from the host, but rewrites 81 and 83 from 46 and 48 (FLIP_SOL includes FLIP_EOS), publishing 1 once a coil has been held two updates, the reverse of the N.C. contact.
mechanisms.label: Lower flippers

mechanisms.behavior: The Flipper (Mini-Right) Assy. 500-5944-02 (printed page 73) with a 22-1080 coil (Q14) and a fluorescent orange mini bat, right of centre above the trough (coil location drawing). Its own N.O. cabinet button (88, DS-5) is read by the CPU, which drives Q14 itself; no end-of-stroke input is wired (the 3-Flipper Circuit draws none, although the assembly heading's item range takes in the EOS switch 180-5149-00) and PinMAME runs no flipper simulation for it. In the gameplay runs holding 88 pulsed Q14. The retained table fires its RightFlipperS from its mini-flipper key handler while the game-on state 15 is set.
mechanisms.label: Mini flipper

mechanisms.behavior: Left (top of the triangle; Q9/49), bottom (Q10/50) and right (Q11/51) turbo bumpers (515-6459-01, -04, -03) with stack-blade spoon switches 180-5015-03; each switch fired its own coil in the gameplay runs. F8 (Q32) lights two #89 at the pops.
mechanisms.label: Three turbo bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left (Q12/59) and right (Q13/62) slingshots (500-5849-01, coil 26-1200, switch 180-5054-00); each switch fired its own coil in the gameplay runs. The retained table's handlers cross the two switch numbers.
mechanisms.label: Slingshots

physical.notes: One G.I. relay on the I/O Power Driver board 520-5137-01 (U206 74HCT273 data latch D0 through R254 1K to Q200 2N3904, coil on 20v DC with D229 across it) switches the 6.3v AC G.I. supply from J14 to four separately fused circuits on J15 (General Illumination Circuit Detailed Wiring Diagram, printed page 89): circuit 1, F24, BRN/WHT to WHT/BRN, under the upper left playfield, 10 #44; circuit 2, F25, YEL to WHT/YEL, under the lower left playfield, 7 #44, plus 2 #555 above the left mid playfield and the left return lane; circuit 3, F26, GRN to WHT/GRN, under the upper right playfield, 7 #44, plus 2 #555 in the coin door; circuit 4, F27, VIO to WHT/VIO, under the lower right playfield, 6 #44, plus 2 #555 above the right ramp and the right return lane. The page warns that G.I. bulb quantities may change during production. The quantity 36 is those 34 playfield bulbs plus the two coin-door bulbs. se.c publishes the relay as GI 0; the harness runs saw it switch on in attract mode and blink with the coins, the ramp exits, the right top lane, the outlanes, the warrior bug target, the bug hole, the VUKs and the drain. The retained table binds it: GICallback = UpdateGI (line 237) calls SetLamp 200 (lines 1155-1159), and UpdateLamps drives the GILamps collection Light001-Light028 and the glow flashers GIFL1 and lfgi001-lfgi004 from channel 200 (lines 1747-1779). Each of the 28 GILamps lights draws its bulb (show_bulb_mesh) and none sits within 0.010 of another, so each is placed as one socket, observed only; the page's string drawing numbers the bulbs per circuit, but the placements have not been matched to it, so no placement carries a circuit. That leaves 28 placed sockets against the 34 playfield bulbs the page prints; the two coin-door bulbs are counted but not placed.
